messages:
maria: Heads-up — I prototyped a small console surface for service accounts that shows per-key routing policies, quota attribution, and a tiny telemetry summary. Wanted to get engineering/security/Product thoughts before I push the mock to the repo.

aj: Nice — can you paste the mock or a screenshot? Curious how much of this is declarative vs inferred from logs.

maria: Pasted the mock here: https://img.redwood/mock-service-perm-1 (simple table: key id, routing policy, quota bucket, recent p50/p95 tokens). The idea is to let a PM or infra owner quickly see why a SA key is hitting fallback routes.

aj: Backend implications: we currently attribute quota by effective_project_id + key_id, but routing policy is computed at the edge (policy engine) and not stored per-request. To show accurate per-key routing we'd need to persist the route decision or surface the policy version used. Two options: 1) store route_decision in the request log (cheap) 2) expose a condensed view from the router service (cheap reads but new API).

maria: prefer 2) if it's not too chatty. We don't want the console to become a log browser.

aj: Agreed. Proposal: add a /v1/keys/:key_id/routing-summary endpoint that returns last N decisions + policy_version + fallback_reason. Example response sketch: ```json
{"policy_version":"2025-03-11-9","decisions":[{"t":"2025-03-11T12:01:02Z","route":"gptq-16-std","fallback":"capacity"}]}
```

samir: Security note: exposing route decisions could leak capacity/topology info. Attackers could infer model placement or capacity hotspots. If we show fallback_reason, we should categorize reasons ("latency/overload/blackout") instead of raw capacity names. Also audit logs must include who viewed the surface.

lina: On UX — keep it high level. Use terms like "routing tier" not internal cluster names. Show a badge for policy_version and a hover for more details. We should add a read-only permission flag: "View key routing & telemetry" so tenants can control who sees it.

aj: Implementation plan: router emits a compact tuple (policy_version, route_slug, reason_code) to telemetry pipeline. We add a cached index (TTL 24h) per key to avoid live lookups. Expose summarized endpoint for console. PR would touch router, telemetry pipeline, and authz.

maria: Samir — do you want to own the authz/audit spec? We'll need a small product-legal note for the UI text about what "routing summary" means.

samir: I can draft. Key points: mask internal cluster identifiers, normalize reasons into categories, log viewer identity, and opt-out for orgs that want no routing telemetry shown.

lina: UX follow-ups: add microcopy: "Routing summaries are derived from recent decisions and may not reflect current capacity" and a link to docs. Minimal table: last route, policy version, last seen time, p50 tokens.

aj: One gotcha: ephemeral keys (short TTL) might not have data. Endpoint should return a clear empty state and suggest checking audit logs or increasing TTL.

maria: Cool. Next steps: @aj file an RFC branch with the endpoint proto + cache plan, @samir produce the authz/audit checklist, @lina iterate on microcopy and the mock. I'll queue a 30m sync after PR/notes if folks prefer.

deploy-bot: deploy 1755556700: router v2.14 rolled to canary (10%). Monitor routing-decisions topic for schema anomalies. :rocket:

aj: I'll start the RFC today. ETA for proto + cache sketch: EOD.

samir: Drafting authz checklist, will drop in #eng-security later today.

lina: Mock updated with microcopy, pushing to the design ticket.

maria: Thanks all — logging this as an action item on the service-perm board. :white_check_mark:
